title: Generic smooth curve and etale boundary after inseparable preparation
statement: Let $S$ be either the spectrum of a field or an excellent integral trait (the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring) [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] dominant finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] morphism $X\to S$, and let $Z\subset X$ be a nowhere dense closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] (its underlying set does not contain the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of $X$). Let $Y$ be an excellent integral scheme with a projective [def-kun-projective] dominant morphism $Y\to S$, let $X_0$ be an excellent integral scheme, let $a:X_0\to X$ be a proper dominant generically finite morphism and $g:X_0\to Y$ a proper dominant morphism such that the composites $X_0\xrightarrow{a}X\to S$ and $X_0\xrightarrow{g}Y\to S$ are equal, and assume that the extension of function fields $\kappa(Y)\subset\kappa(X_0)$ [def-sc-function-field] induced by $g$ has transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then there are an excellent integral scheme $Y_1$ with a projective, proper, dominant, generically finite morphism $b:Y_1\to Y$ such that the composite $Y_1\xrightarrow{b}Y\to S$ is projective and the extension $\kappa(Y)\subset\kappa(Y_1)$ is finite purely inseparable [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], an excellent integral scheme $X_1$, and morphisms $c:X_1\to X_0$ and $f:X_1\to Y_1$ with $g\circ c=b\circ f$, such that $h=a\circ c:X_1\to X$ is proper, dominant and generically finite, $f$ is proper and dominant, and, for the generic point $y_1$ of $Y_1$, the fibre $(X_1)_{y_1}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] irreducible curve over $\kappa(y_1)$ and the fibre $((h^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}})_{y_1}$ of the reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] over $\kappa(y_1)$ (possibly empty). Generically finite means finite over a dense open of the target. Excellence of a scheme means excellence of its affine coordinate rings.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed pp. 163--164: choose a finite purely inseparable extension K/k(Y) such that Nor(X_eta x K) and the reduced boundary are smooth, extend K to a projective alteration Y'->Y, and replace X over Y'. Gabber's 'schematic closure of X_K in X x_Y Y'' is read as the normalization of the dominant component of X_0 x_Y Y_1 (X_K is a normalization, not a subscheme; the closure alone can keep a non-smooth generic fibre, e.g. y^2=x^p-t over F_p(t)). Existence of K: Stacks varieties-lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal and algebra-lemma-make-separable.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $Y$ and put $C=(X_0)_\eta$. The hypothesis $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(Y)}\kappa(X_0)=1$ and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] show that the integral generic fibre $C$ has dimension one. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-geonormal-insep] to the finite-type $\kappa(Y)$-scheme $C$. It supplies a finite purely inseparable extension $K_1/\kappa(Y)$ such that the normalization $N_1$ of $C\times_{\kappa(Y)}K_1$ is geometrically normal over $K_1$. This first extension is chosen only for geometric normality of the normalized curve.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed p. 163

proof.text: First the properties of $N_1$. Since $K_1/\kappa(Y)$ is purely inseparable, $C_{K_1}\to C$ is a homeomorphism (elementary: some power $x\mapsto x^{p^n}$ maps $\mathcal O(C_{K_1})$ into $\mathcal O(C)$ on affine charts, so each prime has exactly one prime above it), hence $C_{K_1}$ is irreducible, $(C_{K_1})_{\mathrm{red}}$ is integral, and $N_1$ is its normalization; [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] makes $N_1\to(C_{K_1})_{\mathrm{red}}$ finite, so $N_1$ is an integral finite-type $K_1$-scheme. Its function field is $\kappa((C_{K_1})_{\mathrm{red}})$, which is algebraic over $\kappa(C)=\kappa(X_0)$ and contains it, so it has transcendence degree one over $K_1$ (elementary, as $K_1/\kappa(Y)$ is algebraic), and [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim N_1=1$. Let $D_1$ be the reduced inverse image in $N_1$ of the generic fibre $(a^{-1}Z)_\eta\subseteq C$. Since $Z$ omits the generic point of $X$ and $a$ is dominant, $a^{-1}Z$ omits the generic point of $X_0$, which is the generic point of $C$; as $N_1\to C$ maps the generic point of the integral $N_1$ to that of $C$, $D_1$ omits the generic point of $N_1$ and is a nowhere-dense closed subscheme of the one-dimensional finite-type scheme $N_1$. Hence [lem-pc-nowhere-dense-dim-zero] gives $\dim D_1\leq0$, and [lem-pc-zero-dimensional-closed-subscheme-finite] makes $D_1$ finite over $K_1$; in particular it has finitely many irreducible components. Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to this finite-type scheme. We obtain a finite purely inseparable extension $K/K_1$ such that $(D_1\times_{K_1}K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is geometrically reduced over $K$. It is finite over $K$, hence the spectrum of a finite reduced $K$-algebra, a finite product of finite field extensions $L/K$; each $L\otimes_K\bar K$ is reduced, so $L/K$ is separable (elementary: an inseparable element has minimal polynomial with a repeated root over $\bar K$, giving a nilpotent in $K(\alpha)\otimes_K\bar K\subseteq L\otimes_K\bar K$). [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion] therefore makes it finite etale over $K$. Thus the second extension is chosen for the boundary and is not inferred from smoothness of the curve.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed pp. 163–164

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-normalization-inseparable-base-change] with $k=\kappa(Y)$, $k_1=K_1$, $k_2=K$ and the integral finite-type $\kappa(Y)$-scheme $C$; its hypothesis is the geometric normality of $N_1$ from step 1. The normalization $N$ of $(C_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is canonically $N_1\times_{K_1}K$ over $C_K$, it is geometrically normal over $K$, and the reduced inverse image of $D_1$ in it is $(D_1\times_{K_1}K)_{\mathrm{red}}$; since reduced inverse images depend only on underlying sets, this is also the reduced inverse image of $(a^{-1}Z)_\eta$ in $N$. Its dimension is one: $N$ is integral (it is the normalization of the integral scheme $(C_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$) and of finite type over $K$ (a base change of $N_1$), and its function field is algebraic over $\kappa(X_0)$ and contains it, so it has transcendence degree one over the algebraic extension $K$ of $\kappa(Y)$; [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim N=1$. This supplies both the normalized curve and the boundary model to be spread over $Y$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed pp. 163–164; normalization after the further purely inseparable extension

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-inseparable-spread-normalization] to $Y$, $X_0$, $g$, the chosen $K/\kappa(Y)$, and the given proper dominant generically finite $a:X_0\to X$. We obtain an excellent integral $Y_1$, a finite projective proper dominant generically finite $b:Y_1\to Y$ with $Y_1\to S$ projective and $\kappa(Y_1)\cong K$, an excellent integral $X_1$, and maps $c:X_1\to X_0$ and $f:X_1\to Y_1$ with $g\circ c=b\circ f$. It also gives that $h=a\circ c$ is proper dominant generically finite and identifies the generic fibre $(X_1)_{y_1}$ with the normalization of the corresponding dominant component after the field extension $K$.

source.place: Expose X, proof of Theorem 3.5, Step 5, printed pp. 163–164

proof.text: The generic fibre in step 4 is the normalized one-dimensional component identified in step 3 and is geometrically normal over $\kappa(y_1)\cong K$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-geonormal-dim-one-smooth] makes $(X_1)_{y_1}$ smooth and geometrically reduced. The dominant component used in the normalization is integral, so its normalization is nonempty and connected; the irreducibility clause of that lemma gives that $(X_1)_{y_1}$ is an irreducible curve. Under the same identification, the reduced inverse image $((h^{-1}Z)_{\mathrm{red}})_{y_1}$ is $(D_1\times_{K_1}K)_{\mathrm{red}}$, which was shown finite etale over $K$ in step 2. The empty boundary case is included.

split_report.summary: Compared the imported statement with Exposé X, Theorem 3.5 Step 5 and repaired the false separability inference. The proof now chooses K1 to make the normalized generic curve geometrically normal, chooses a further finite purely inseparable K/K1 using the finite-inseparable geometric-reduction lemma for the reduced boundary, and invokes an explicit normalization base-change node before spreading K projectively. The generic fibre dimension is derived from the one-dimensional generic fibre and finite birational normalization, and the boundary is proved finite etale from geometric reducedness and the finite-etale algebra criterion.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the initial finite purely inseparable normalization choice in Step 5; Step 2 realizes the additional purely inseparable extension needed for the reduced boundary; Step 3 realizes normalization compatibility and dimension; Step 4 realizes extension to a projective alteration; Step 5 realizes the smooth irreducible curve and finite etale boundary conclusions.

tool_uses.why: Steps 1 and 3 use the transcendence-degree dimension formula for the generic fibre and dimension preservation calculation; no node in sk-i-curve-zero supplies this formula.
Step 1 uses the generic finite purely inseparable extension whose normalized curve is geometrically normal; this normalization theorem is supplied from sec-proper-base-change.
Step 2 uses the finite purely inseparable extension making a finite-type scheme reduction geometrically reduced; this field-preparation lemma is supplied from sec-smooth-purity.
Step 5 uses the dimension-one geometrically normal implies smooth and geometrically reduced criterion; this generic field criterion is supplied from sec-proper-base-change.
Step 2 uses the dimension-zero consequence for a nowhere-dense boundary in a curve; this dimension lemma is supplied from sec-picard-framework.
Step 2 uses zero-dimensional finite-type boundary to obtain finiteness over the generic residue field; this finiteness lemma is supplied from sec-picard-framework.

Steps 2 and 5 use the finite algebra criterion identifying a finite geometrically reduced algebra with a finite product of finite separable fields; this algebra lemma is supplied from sec-abelian-varieties.

Step 2 (added on review) takes only finiteness of the normalization of a reduced finite-type scheme over a field, to make N_1 of finite type over K_1; no node of sk-i-curve-zero states this generic finiteness fact.
